Payloads: sunrise punta cana, d.r. i had read many of the reviews of the grand paradise before leaving with my wife, two daughters and son-in-law and frankly was concerned. we arrived in punta cana with no luggage. none for the five of us. they had overbooked the rooms and sent us to their second hotel/time-share area called the club. it seemed things were going downhill fast. our ground transportation was provided by turinter and their representative, noel, did everything possible to locate the luggage. with his assistance, the luggage arrived the following day on the next flight. the club was a blessing in disguise. the rooms were very large with a jacuzzi. our balcony faced east, so the items set out were dry by 9 am. the pool at the club had a swim up bar and the best bar was at the mangler restaraunt area where they actually made mixed drinks. the other great bar was at the main hotel, upstairs. i believe i attended six bars in all. a train ran frequently to shuttle between the two resort locations. not a big deal.our standard breakfast was at the international where they served a continental style breakfast and you could also order off the menu. excellent omelets. at the main resort a full buffet was available, we just did not feel like eating that much. we had supper twice at the international, once the italian and once chinese. each exceeded my expectations, not gourmet, but very tasty. service was great, not always fast, but always with a willing spirit. fresh fruit at every meal. take a pair or two of long pants for the evening sit down restaurants, no shorts allowed.the staff genuinely liked to be helpful. most of the waiting and service people spoke english and french. they work long hours each day and 26 days a month. tips of any size were appreciated though not expected. we took two dollar bills which got attention, they said it was good luck. maybe it was good luck to get two dollars rather than one.the resort has a real european flair. many french. we also met people from canada, lichtenstein, germmany, spain and russia. toplessness was practiced on the beach area, only seldom around the pools. even at that, you had to look to find a topless bather. frankly the beach and sea was so spectacular you did not notice.we drank the water provided with the meals and a fresh gallon of water was provided to our room each day. we re-filled our small bottles a few times. dad used the imodium the last day, the others were fine.it is a great place to come if you are a couple or large family. they can accommo

Payloads: river ranch is great, hotel needs a lot of help having just returned from the hilton squaw peak, i must say that this hotel has major problems. nowehere on the website does it indicaqte that the property is undergoing major renovations, but it is. we traveled with 4 other families. two of the rooms had air conditioner problems, requiring a move. the moves took at least an hour to accomplish, and, one move required the guests to move their own luggage, as the bellman refused to move the bags, after being asked not to drag the ladies' dress on the ground. we were told that the bell station moves about 40 rooms a day due to the construction, and problems with the rooms. half the hotel is closed, for construction, leaving only two ice machines an entire wing. this meant that there was hardly any ice ever available. the elevator broke during our stay. since there was only one elevator in the south wing, if you wanted to get to and from your room, you had to walk.the pool is very nice, and the kids enjoyed it. the south pool was closed, and we did not get to the north pool. a fire, or what was described as an event, in lanatanna caused the only restaurant to be the hole in the wall.overall, the service in the hotel is poor. the river ranch is great, but, the hotel itself does not seem to be hilton quality. more like comfort inn quality.

Payloads: good deal for the money we booked two rooms, which weree both comfortable and spacious. a/c worked well. loved the lighting - lamps turned on and up and off with a mere touch. bed was ultra comfortable. the decor is contemporary and fun. the location was very convenient for us as we needed to be near ucla. breakfast was very good, excellent coffee, and the restaurant has a fun, sleek decor. negatives - our tub drain was clogged and slow (room 827), the walls are a bit thin (our neighbors came in at 3am and we could literally hear their entire conversation), and the ceiling in the fitness room is low, so my 6'4 husband couldn't use the treadmill. we didn't complain about the tub because we only stayed one night, and the other things weren't anything that management could fix anyway, so we didn't report those either (this is being written in case management reads this and wonders why we didn't report anything while we were there).that being said, we would still stay here again. i shopped around for prices and what we could get here with our aaa discount was quite a bit better than anything else i could find of the same quality and location.

Payloads: local entertainment stayed at this holiday inn pre cruise with my wife and 2 children for the second time in two years. this hotel is located across from bayside as others have posted and makes it easy to get a meal and do some walking around the shops. when staying at this hotel you should be made aware that if there is any type of entertainment at bayside or the venue next to bayside and you have a room facing the port....it will be extremely noisy until about 2:00 in the am. since staying here the first time i inquired about any events happening when making this booking and was advised that none were scheduled. upon check in i asked again if any events would be happening during our stay and again told that nothing was scheduled. low and behold there was an event with extremely loud music which started at 8:00 and lasted until past 2:00 am. contacting management i found out that in fact the hotel did know of this event, but somehow had failed to notify their employees?????? management did compensate our bill for the inconvience which was appreciated, but it made for a very long night. listed below is personnal insight.1) this hotel is located in downtown (which is dirty) and is approx $20.00 cab ride to port2) no grocery store within the area3) liquor store 2 blks from hotel (expensive)4) elevator's are small, book a room on top floor to eliminate long waits 5) after talking with cabbie's found out that south beach is about 20 minutes away but if you stay on a weekend and drive or take a cab to south beach it could take over an hour due to traffic6) good breakfast bar7) port facing rooms have a great view of ships (freedom of the seas)(especially if you are awake when it arrives in the early am)

Payloads: wonderful hotel i made reservations at the palomar partly because of the good reviews here. it exceeded our expectations.nice room, everything looked new and spotlessly clean. neat modern arty decor. we got a complimentary upgrade to a room with beautiful view of la from the 17th floor. the bed was big and comfy with a bunch of fluffy pillows and a really warm comforter (actually too warm). most comfortable bed i've ever slept on in a hotel. the staff was great. we didn't need them much, but they were friendly, helpful and efficient when we did. the two nights we were there, the room was extremely quiet. probably due to the high floor we were on and not many people being around. some people have noted that the a/c is very noisy. in our room, it wasn't. we could hear it turning on, but the sound was not loud by any stretch. nice touches - 42 lcd hd tv, large room safe, plush bath robes, high quality shampoo/conditioner. the hotel is in a good location. we caught a movie at the theatre a safe two block walk away. or you can walk to westwood village. drive down wilshire blvd. and there are a ton of stores and restaurants. hop on the freeway to the getty center (which we did and had a great time) or santa monica beach. a few nits - you cannot control the water flow in the sink faucet, only the temperature. more than a few times, i ended up splashing water all over the place due to the high water pressure. you hang up towels to reuse, but they get replaced anyway. parking is $30 a day, valet only. that didn't bother me much though given the low room rate.we got the aaa rate of $161 a night on a holiday weekend. what a great deal! we really enjoyed our stay. highly recommended.

Payloads: Paradise Found! We returned from a glorious vacation at Ocean Sands on March 24, 2006. I have travelled to tropical locales five times, so although far from being worldly, I do have some experiences with which to compare. I would say this resort deserves it's 4+ rating...in a 3rd world country. I am, unfortunately, an extreme clean freak, and this resort suited me just fine! We were fortunate enough to be given a VIP room in Villa 10, with both ocean and pool views...only steps to the beach. So perhaps my review would be different if I had stayed in Villa 1, facing the empty lot or opposite resort. I can't judge that, as I never saw any other rooms except the one we were given on the last day to shower in, before our flight left. It was not too pleasing as it had a dismal view and was a smoking room....however it was still clean and had a lovely marble washroom with double sinks, shower and jacuzzi. Enough of the room....who cares? Believe me you will never be in it! The ocean is WARM and a stunning turquoise. The sand is powdery fine and literally, stretches endlessly in BOTH directions! We walked 2 hours north one day and 2 hours south another. Both times we had to return due to heat exhaustion,but we wanted to KEEP going....but there was no end in sight!! We found a beautiful clear lagoon to swim in when we walked north, and the day we walked south we discovered some beautiful spots for photos (some secluded, swaying palm trees that had a perfect backdrop for photos). Do not envision a secluded paradise...it is a paradise but FAR from secluded!!! We were there at Spring Break so we expected a lot of tourists...and there were! What I did not like about the resorts at Punta Cana was the fact that there is a STEADY stream of speedboats, banana boats, parachute boats,water taxis, helicopters etc. etc. They speed about with no spotters and little regard to safety, so it is definitely swimmers beware!!! At times I felt we were in a war zone because of the continual drone of the helicopters overhead, carrying tourists. However, it did not ruin our vacation and our teenage son LOVED all the action so we went with the flow. Truly, the gorgeous weather, warm turquoise ocean, clean resort and endless sretches of talcumy sand more than make up for any shortcomings! We had perfect weather the entire week. Payloads: a pleasant surprise! i wasn't quite sure what to expect at the beverly garland, but it was definitely better than i thought it would be after reading some of the reviews posted here. the overall impression that greeted me on arriving was that it was quite dated. the reception staff were very helpful, and the staff in the gift/tour shop were extremely friendly and helpful. the room, on first impressions, was pretty cramped, but adequate, clean, and comfortable. we were put in the annex building which overlooked the freeway. the noise wasn't a problem, unless you left the balcony door open. the complimentry wi-fi connection for my laptop was excellent. we had a toilet blockage, but the maintenance man was there within 10 minutes to fix it (this was at 10 pm). the restaurant at the front (tula's) served some excellent food, and had an outdoor area where you could eat / drink when the weather was nice..which we did. you could also order room service from here. you would definitely need a car if you wanted to go shopping, as the nearest mall was about 10 mins away by car and the hotel is a bit isolated, unless you are planning to go to universal (the hotel runs a regular free shuttle throughout the day). we were only here for two nights as a stopover travelling from australia, new zealand and fiji, and we did a tour to tijuana on one day (which is another story), so did not feel the need to hire a car. overall, it was ok.

Payloads: great hotel, and good location to explore. we stayed here for 4 nights as part of our trip away to get married. so you can imagine, i wanted everything to be just right for our special trip! also, allow enough time for the alcatraz visit we were there for hours, and thought we would be in and out within the hour.

Payloads: Wonderful second honeymoon Me and my husband stayed from 1 - 15 August. We were very worried having read so many bad reviews but decided the holiday would be what we made it. We got married at the Riu Tropical Bay in Jamaica in February with 31 guests so this holiday was a sort of second honeymoon by ourselves. The Riu is a five star and we both agreed that there wasn't much difference in the quality of the two hotels. We honestly can't understand how people can write such horrible things. Our check in was quick, we were given a room upgrade for being honeymooners and the bellboy took us with our bags straight to our room. Within a minute of closing the door there was a knock on the door and we were brought a fruit basket and a bottle of rum (all for being honeymooners). We were given an ocean view (room 2412). The room was nice and clean, the bathroom was very big and clean and we always had fresh towels and had our fridge refilled every day without having to ask. One day our tv broke. We called down to reception just before going out to dinner and by the time we got back it had been fixed. The grounds of the hotel are lovely and very well maintained. The beach is gorgeous. We spent every day on the beach. The pool looks very nice but it was always very busy and full of kids which wasn't what we wanted on our honeymoon. We swam in the pool one day but the water was very warm. The sea was much more refreshing and the waves were a lot of fun. We ate at the buffet every day for breakfast and found it fine. I found it a bit limited for lunch but that was mainly because I was being very wary of what I ate having read all the reviews about illness. Both me and my husband got through the entire stay without a hint of illness. One of us has always had something on every holiday we have been on except this one. We tried to book the speciality restaurants as much as possible. It made more of a night out than just going to the buffet. Payloads: a 3-star hilton, not a 4-star resort this hotel has very nice rooms -- it's an all-suite property with excellent new beds. (in fact, i would give the hilton beds nearly equal marks with westin's heavenly versions.) but the rest of the property is bland. think of a suburban version of a standard hilton city location with a nice pool that is well landscaped. a couple of significant complaints: $12 per day to use the gym is out-of-hand, especially when factoring the cost of the room. also, i'm very sorry but guests should not be penalized by kitchen renovations. twice i had to send food back from room service for poor quality.

Payloads: kind of scary when arriving past dark my daughter and i booked on this island thinking it would be closer to the airport for my departure early in the morning. it isn't really closer than kowloon, since you have to go over the mountain by taxi or bus. we arrived after dark by taxi, and since there is no beach front road, we had to walk down a one block alley with our luggage. it was dark and there were street people sleeping in the alley, a bit scarry for 2 american females. once we got to the hotel, it was okay. not the best, but i was tired of spending money, and it was cheap. somewhat like a motel 6 in the usa. once you figure in the taxi fare, (yes, i know we could have taken the ferry, but we had a lot of luggage and thought a taxi was the way to go) both to the hotel and back again in the morning, we could have stayed at the regal at the airport. we only stayed the one night, it was okay, but last minute booking at the regal airport hotel would have been just as cheap, without the hassel of the taxi. i will say that it would be a nice place to stay with a family, a good base to see hong kong from. cheap, not awful, and the people were very friendly. i would like to have seen the place in the day time. we arrived at dark and left in the dark. up

The hotel is located in a new conference complex about 15 minutes outside of the city center. So if you want to walk out your door to La Rambla, you should stay elsewhere. Payloads: great staff we stayed here for two nights in early june. i was very pleased with the hotel. the room was small, i guess because we had booked under a government rate, so they probably gave us the smallest they had. it was on the top (the 4th) floor, though. a view of the courtyard, which seems to be an inaccessible small yard with some trees planted and a net on top, so no birds to watch. the bed was very comfy, the minibar well stocked and the tv worked. the room was very clean and the shower had one of the curved curtain rods, so plenty of room.the front desk staff was great, helpful on check-in, had supply of extra coffee supplies for the room and stamps for purchase, offered to mail our postcards, and the concierge desk seemed very busy. we didn't use them, but people over there looked happy and satisfied. the wine in the evening was nice (go early or you will miss appetizers), as was the coffee and (very small) biscottis in the morning. my husband wanted a more substantial breakfast. great location, if you are doing north and east san francisco stuff. walking distance to the wharf, the north beach area (great food!!!) and the alcatraz ferry dock.

Payloads: satisfactory stay for the right price we recently stayed atthe embassy suites north at lax. we had to stay for 2 nights to visit family in la before boarding a cruise ship in san pedro (port of los angeles). we were travelling with 2 teenage children so wanted the two room suite and breakfast buffet option. we got a rate of 125.00 for first night and 139.00 for second night through aaa which i thought was good for the amount of space. 2 queen beds and 1 pull out couch.we arrived at 11 pm and found the hotel shuttle right outside from the baggage carousel. make sure you are getting on the embassy suites lax north shuttle as there is another embassy suites lax south which is confusing. the shuttle we took also serviced the marriott which i found odd but perhaps it was the late evening arrival. even with a stop at the marriott first it only took 5 to 7 minutes to be delivered right to the front door of the hotel. check in was very easy but we had missed the food room service hours and they did not serve any food at the restaurant or room service after 11 pm. i thought i had read that they had 24 hour room service so my hubby was not happy. they did have a little market and he bought some really gross burritos and even grosser cheese pizzas for the kids to microwave in the room -- $38.00 dollars worth to be exact.we were on the second floor which was pretty easy but now about the room. just know that the first impression of the room was really not good and i was wanting to ask for another room but as mentioned above i had a very hungry and tired family who had been fllying for 8 hours and were still dealing with the time change which made it like 4 am so we settled for what we were given. the rug was musty smelling and there was a 24 inch diameter red stain on the rug in the bedroom. the tub in the bathroom looked oldish and scratched and never looked as though it had been cleaned. just tired and old finish i think. the linens and beds were clean and Payloads: birthday getaway in april i took my husband to the royal palms for a birthday getaway from a th-monday. i had researched many resorts and had narrowed my choices to the lake austin spa resort and the royal palms. the royal palms was clearly a more interesting destination with options outside of the resort that were endless, so i chose it. i booked through expedia and while the rp was either the most expensive or 2nd most expensive choice in the phx/scottsdale area, it seemed to be the best fit. the descriptions on this site and at the rp website indicated it's small and personal feel and service, which was appealing. the website won me over with the awards list and the beautiful photos, especially those showing it's proximity to camelback mtn. i booked the package (air and hotel) well in advance- at least 4 months and figured i would begin making spa, restaurant and excursion reservations about one month out. long story short, it is very important to call in advance (as soon as you book would be best) in order to get your preferred times to dine at t. cooks for dinner (breakfast and lunch res. not required) and especially at the spa. the times i had asked for intitially were unavailable, even one month in advance. also, when you speak to someone, take their name and then call again a few weeks before your trip to confirm your appts. it was all worked out before we arrived and we were welcomed with fabulous service, but i felt like most of that was due to my frequent contact beforehand. be sure plan ahead if you stay at the rp...your trip will only be worth the expense if you plan each detail so as not to miss out on all of the opportunities and inclusions in staying here. the only reasons i did not give this resort a full 5 are: although the resort does not claim to be adults only, all of the reviews and even the rp website alludes to this. we were there during a insurance broker's conference and many brokers had brought their children with them. while this was only a minor issue, it is worth noting that at a resort with a pool area that is so intimate, children's voices (even joyful ones) carry and tend to interfere slightly with the romantic and peaceful atmosphere.even when you book ahead of time, the charges in the spa are a) never the same as what you saw online or were quoted and b) always seemingly random (literally as if the numbers were simply drawn from a lottery) and way over-priced. check your bill carefully. if you speak to someone in charge, they will correct the bill, but it will be time consuming. the spa is fabulous and while i am willing to pay $500 a night for a room, paying more than $150 for a very standard 60 minute massage is ridiculous. thinking that i would have been disappointed with only one day at the spa, i booked two mornings full of spa activities and services on the 2nd and 4th days of our stay. if i could do it all over again, i would simply ask for the 90 minute massage (confirm the price in writing ahead of time) and leave the spa treatments to that. this was worth every penny. the 60 minute massage and manicure were overpriced and not nearly relaxing or enjoyable enough to justify the price. i found myself anxious the entire time i should have been enjoying these treatments b/c i knew that i was spending hundreds of dollars on something that had less than $100 of value to me. on the last day we stayed, a motley crew of people that looked as if they belonged in a trashy music video took over the pool. they ordered grey goose and champagne as if it were going out of style (beginning before noon) and played their loud music and smoked their cigarettes while dancing their scantily clad bodies around the pool. they even brought their yapper of a dog to run around wildly and bother the guests. while these folks obviously had paid (on credit no doubt) for the two cabanas they inhabited it didn't matter b/c the size of the pool and area were only modestly larger than a large residential pool. please also keep in mind that the past few days (while many children had been present) were quite peaceful and the pool had only been visited by folks with similar interests (sunbathing, having maybe 1 or 2 drinks and lunch and enjoyng the peaceful and romantic atmosphere). while rick was fab. by asking them to keep quiet and not physically invade the other guest's space, there was nothing he could do but keep bringing them their drinks and grin and bear it. needless to say, we did not stay at the pool more than 5 minutes on our last day, which was disappointing. i am not sure how the rp could have prevented this occurance, but i am shocked that those sorts of people chose the rp for their party. it certainly was not a good match!thanks are deserved! the special touches at the rp are what makes it worth the cost. while you could stay at the bellagio for less, no one there will remember your name, which pool chair you like or whether you prefer red or white. you certainly won't be receiving personally signed notes at the beginnning and end of your stay, nor rose petal covered bedding or chocolate covered strawberries as a surprise at turn-down. the staff was superb and especially gracious and friendly. the grounds are beautiful. the food and service are great. the suite is worth the extra $- having the extra room is great for couples with different sleeping habits.tips: place a personal item on a pool chair early in the morning to get your preferred spot. (the sun is strong, so be sure to wear sunscreen at all times.) be sure to go to camelback mtn. for a few hikes- the ones recommended in the brochure are great- for all levels. sunset horsesback riding is highly recommended. while the crowd you'll be with for 4 hours isn't the classiest, the views are breathtaking. go to arizona-horses for one option. skip the shopping, especially if you live in a more metropolitan area. t. cooks is as good as any restaurant off site, so if i had it to do again i would have dined there each evening i was interested in a more formal meal. for informal, do a steakhouse or cookout with the horseback riding and be sure to check out pizza bianco. the bar bianco and pizza rest. are well worth the wait. it is such a cute set-up on a lovely evening. also, you'll be right next to the stadium, so you can check that out, too. if you decide to rent a car (which you don't need to do unless you plan to leave the resort more than once per day), def. do the convertible. we did and did not regret it.

Payloads: some disappointments we'd heard a lot of good things about the tuscan inn from people who'd stayed there for a night or two before cruising out of the port of san francisco. normally we'd stay at the sf hilton, or one of the marriott properties, but we decided this time to try something else.the tuscan inn room was quite nicely appointed, the bed was comfortable the chairs tv adequate, the bathroom reasonably good. street noise can be a problem in an outside room, though, and the window coverings (sliding roman blinds that don't quite meet) left a lot to be desired if you don't want to get up with the sun.housekeeping service was very inadequate, though. we left the room at 10:30 am, placing the please make up room tag in the key slot. there were at least 4, and maybe 6, housekeeping carts between our room the elevator. yet when we returned at 3:30 the room hadn't been touched! the attached restaurant (cafe pescadore) is open for breakfast with a fairly skimpy menu - but quite good coffee.on balance, it was an ok place to stay but, perhaps, not to return to. it's fine if it's convenient to what you're doing in the city.

Payloads: good location and excellent service. not perfect, however... i booked the sofitel for a one-night stay on a mid-week business trip to los angeles. the hotel is nicely situated directly across from the beverly center, one of la's best shopping malls. good food and sightseeing options are right outside the door, which is rare for la.the hotel is modern and hip with very well kept grounds and an impressive entry area. the rooms are also modern in appearance with flat panel tvs and sharp, clean decor.i found the service to be superior, from the reception to the valet parking attendants. no issues at check-in. check-out or anywhere in between.consistent with earlier reviews, the room i was given was very small for the states. if i was with my wife, we would have been cramped. but, for one, the size was fine. i also found the room to be otherwise spotless and comfortable, with a good view of the busy la street scene below. the bed was comfortable and i slept well.so, in all, i would recommend the sofitel for travelers to la or those on business. it is well located and can be a good value, especially if you shop around on discount internet websites.

Payloads: perfect airport hotel my husband and i stayed at this hotel for 1 night in september after a long haul flight. we wanted somewhere comfortable, that was near the airport so we could pick up the hire car easily the next morning. the holiday inn fitted the bill perfectly, the price is very reasonable considering the size of the rooms and the hotel staff are happy to arrange free shuttle transfers to and from the airport or car hire depot. our room was a king suite, was very clean and had a huge, extremely comfortable bed. we weren't very hungry so the waffle house next door to the hotel was sufficient for us, apparently there is a restaurant in the hotel next door for more substantial meals. the complimentary breakfast is very nice and has a wide selection of breads, pastries and cereals, as well as eggs and bacon. check-in was fast and efficient and the staff were helpful and friendly. there is a pc in the foyer which guests can use to access the internet. if you're looking for a hotel near the airport before or after a flight then i highly recommend the holiday inn.

Payloads: great inexpensive hotel in heart of sf we were very happy with our stay here. the rooms are very small, we didn't have a view (except of a brick wall), but we stayed in the center of sf for less than $70 a night, and that's hard to beat. this hotel is more in the european style - the room is not where you will be spending most of your time, so why bother making it huge?everything was clean enough that we were comfortable. the free breakfast was good enough to get your day started, and the staff was helpful all the time, and friendly most of the time. we have already recommended this hotel to several of our friends and acquaintances and will return when we next go to sf.

Payloads: great experience we stayed here for 4 nights for $125 from hotwire. the first night we were on the street, and could here motorcycles racing all night. we complained, and were moved to a quiet room for the duration of our stay. on the morning of the second day my daughter had stomach cramps and we had to go to the emergency room. we left at 6:30 am, and the front desk and valet had a cab ready with instructions on where to go by the time we came down the elevator. we were very impressed with the service we received. the location for tourists can not be beat. you are 2 blocks from the wharf, the mason line cable car is right behind the hotel, the f line street car is a block away, and pier 39 and the alcatraz tour is with in walking distance. there is a trader joes, safeway, and walgreens close by too.the rooms were nice, comfortable, and clean. the shower was great. i am still missing the strong coffee and biscotti we had for breakfast every morning. the next time we are in sf, we will be staying at the tuscan inn again.

Payloads: great location what a great hotel in a great city. my wife and i arrived from the east coast at 11 am and the front desk found us a room that had already been cleaned and was ready. that was great to since we had been up so early and needed a place to freshen up. the location is convenient to chinatown and union square, just a couple of blocks each way. the trolley line has a stop right beside the hotel and that makes it easy to get to all the tourist spots. a newspaper and coffee or tea in the morning is waiting at your door. the hotel is very clean and the staff was very accommodating. the room was a little outdated, but the very plush and comfortable bed more that made up for that one flaw.

wait in line for the business service roomcheckout - fast, but getting a taxi seemed tough-----------------------the details-----------------------parking i used the holiday inn for an overnight stay before a cruise. we drove in from out of town and, while the hotel website advertises $12 parking, they neglected to mention that they had all of 20-30 parking spaces for their 10 story hotel. there are other downtown pay parking lots near by, but it leaves you unloading, hunt for a space somewhere and walking back.... in a downtown environment that had the hotel put up a 8' fence with gates around the lot (if they worry, then i worry).in my case, after finding a lot that i could park in and unloading my car, someone happened to have left the hotel lot so i was able to snag a space.check-inthe hotel lobby is nicely appointed with what seemed to be a nice bar/dining area (we didn't eat there). check-in was easy and polite.baggageas with most such hotels, getting a luggage cart without a bellman attached proved to be a challenge. he keeps it/them tucked away in a closet behind his desk. after first asking just for a cart, i reconsidered and agreed to have him help with the bags (it was a bit of a maze to get from the parking, around the pool and then zig-zag through the service area of the hotel).unfortunately, i tried 5 times to tell him i would like him to help us, but i only speak english and wasn't able to get the idea across to him in miami's native tounge. so we took the cart and hauled it up ourselves. to his credit, the bellman smiled a lot and seemed friendly enough.no comissarythey don't have any of the usual razor, shampoo, soap, aspirin.... stuff that most hotels have. if you've left a anything at home, you'll need to go out to a drug store (closest was 4 blocks down).the roomthe halls were nice but the room smelled and had significant signs of water damage and peeling wallpaper. the bathroom door had been painted so many times that it couldn't be closed. the entryway to the room is a tight hallway that barely fits you with a suitcase and can't fit the luggage cart, so you have to unload from the hallway and drag things in.the churchour room was on the side that was separated from a church by a small road . at 7am, the church loudspeakers started chiming out christmas music right into our room. that went on for 30 minutes of clanging and gonging. get a room on another side of the building if you like to sleep in.internet, or lack thereofi had some things i needed to do just before leaving, and tried to use the their advertised free wireless internet. it wasn't even recognizable in my room at all (5th floor, north side). i called down and they said i should go to the business services room on the second floor. it was packed with all the other people who couldn't get in from their rooms.i went to the lobby, where i'd seen someone using a laptop. i could find the network but it was up and down enough to rival the waves at the beach. after fighting for 20 minutes to connect at all, i couldn't stay connected long enough to do much of anything. i finally went back to the business services room and found a spot. i managed to download the cell-phone dialer software i needed to tie my computer to my cell phone and use it's internet connection to connect with my office and get my work done.don't count on the net there.checkoutthe room was already paid, so it's a leave-the-card-on-the-dresser-and-go checkout, which is nice. we had a car, so we loaded up and were out. there was what seemed to be a taxi-waiting-line in the hotel lobby that extended all the way back to the dining room (30+ people w/bags). i was glad i didn't need a ride.conclusionit serves as a need to crash somewhere better than my car, but the next time i'm in miami for a cruise or any reason other than a stay at a resort on the beach trip, i plan on staying at a (hopefully nicer) outlying hotel and drive the 10-20 minutes into the downtown area if i need to hop the ship.

Payloads: great location at a reasonable price my wife and i took two trips to san fran in 2004 and stayed at the best western both times. the first was for a week in january. the hotel location was great. we flew in to san fran airport, took the bart downtown, and then took a cable car to a stop 1 block from the hotel. we didnt have or need a car so we didnt have to deal with parking a car i believe it is $30 a day-- par for the city. the hotel is clean and neat, our room was clean and comfortable. if i had to be critical the room could use a little updateing, but not a big deal. the front desk was friendly, however not terribly knowledgeable--i would assume high turnover. the location is great, if your an active person you can walk everywhere from this hotel, in fact we took a long run up the shore --crissy field and accross the golden gate bridge. north beach starts a block away and heads north, we skipped the touristy fishermans warf area. restaurants are everywhere, however we did not eat at the tuscan restaurant in the hotel. as far as convenience--the cable car stop is 1 block away and that along with the outstanding bus system will get you everywhere you need to go. we plan on visiting the city often, and we plan on staying at this location for the foreseeable future.

Payloads: what an amazing place - magic! we have just arrived back from 5 stunning days at the ritz carlton in bali. we had initially booked an ocean view suite, however when we arrived were told taht they had over booked these particular rooms so they had to upgrade us to a cliff top villa! it was heaven!the grounds of the ritz carton are breath-taking! it is set high on a cliff with green, soft grass areas and crystal cleaqr pools spread all over. the most impressive pool was the one which was set in the cliff side, with views spanning out over the indian ocean. from the pool you could look down to the private beach or out for miles into the ocean. it was a magical place to sit and have a cocktail by the pool in the late afternoon.we ate at the italian restaurant on the first night we were there. the food was reasonable and the menu was quite extensive. i wouldn't rave about the food and the restaurant was quite empty, without much atmosphere so it wasn't the best night, however it was great that we could just walk from our villa to the restaurant in 5 minutes flat and not have to worry about leaving the grounds. there were some local guys serenading the few guests that were dining with u2 and elvis prestly. it was very sweet!my only suggestion, given that i spoke with other guests at the resort, would be to stay in a villa if at all possible. i don't think the experience would have been quite the same if we were staying in a standard room. i heard that some of the rooms are quite out

Payloads: terrible service my husband and i stayed at the biltmore on our wedding night. we booked this as a special treat to ourselves because we could not afford a honeymoon since we are both graduate students. since we are both history buffs, we booked the biltmore for its historical value and it seemed like the closest we could get to european grandeur without having to go to europe (or vegas, heaven forbid).like others have stated, the entrance of the hotel is spectacular and the pictures speak for themselves. we booked a standard room but we were hoping to get a free room upgrade as most similar-class hotels provide this service for new bride and grooms. in fact, nearly all of our friends received free room upgrades and complimentary champagne and strawberries on their wedding nights in similar hotels in the area such as the hilton, westin, intercontinental, and the hyatt.we walked in with our full wedding attire and received many congratulations from random people. however, we were only met with rudeness with the concierge. the service was curt, there was no mention of congratulation, and when we asked if any kind of upgrades or services were available, the front desk person seemed appalled that we should even ask. when we mentioned our friends who had received this service at the omni recently, they said, well then maybe you should have booked at the omni.we were not expecting or demanding any kind of upgrade; we just inquired based upon the experiences of our other married friends. the fact that we were rebuffed in such a rude way was a major sore spot on our wedding night. the room we did end up staying in was almost offensive for the price we paid- we have even stayed in nicer hostels in europe for a fraction of the price. my husband felt sorry that we had to spend our wedding night like this and we were very close to getting another room at the bonaventure just down the street. we have stayed in their rooms and although they are small, the furnishings and decor are up to par with a 4 star hotel. we even called the bonaventure from our biltmore hotel room to inquire about room availabilities, and when we asked about services for new bride and grooms, the concierge replied professionally and guaranteed that yes, the bonaventure always provides room upgrades for bride and grooms based on room availability, and we would have definitely received a suite if we had booked that evening. we ultimately decided not to book since we were so exhausted from the wedding and we didn't want to have to pay another $35 for valet parking on top of a wasted hotel night fee.the grand days of the biltmore are certainly behind it. judging by the service, you can tell that the hotel is struggling as it cannot keep up with its competitors in standard measures of hospitality. downtown los angeles is rapidly developing and ironically, the once swanky and fashionable biltmore will not be able to keep up with its gentrifying surroundings.

Payloads: mixed feelings... not like last year hi there...this is my second posting, my previous one was for the princess resort, which is next door.now bear in mind that my review will be as objective as possible considering we've experienced a great week last year and a not-so-great one this year. my review is objective in the sense that i will compare last year's experience with this present year but with the special circumstances that affected this year's trip, they are:hurricane jeanne:jeanne threw a fit around punta cana, by talking with the local people outside of the resort and keeping in mind the exchange rate and the prices of various essential commodities; jeanne did a lot of damage to the infrastructures (roofs and some buildings) since they are not adapted to the hurricane-force winds. some resorts were closed and their booked clients were relocated to open resorts, causing congestion of the equipment, workforce and hotel infrastructures. bottom-line: the hurricane did a lot of damage; hotels, resorts and tour operators underestimated the damage; sent their clinets to open resorts as to minimize financial loses but these resorts had staff only for their low-season period. some staff membres were just transplanted from other (closed) resorts and had no idea of the policies and procedures of their employers resulting in a lot of eroneous information to customers.sickness:upon departure for the resort, out tour operator representative informed us that more than half of the clients staying at our resort have been sick during the saty and that this did not occur in any other resort in punta cana during that same period.i myslef was sick for 4 days and took my prescription of cipro on the 3rd day of sickness because of the gut-wrnching cramps. (note ot all the people who say that bringing antibiotics is superfluous: i'm never sick during travel and i've experienced pain to incredible levels in my life so i'm not one that complains about belly-aches. i would like to see how you endure these cramps during your holidays).on the first day i got sick i noticed (talking with other guests) that a lot of people were sick too and upon further investigation, the sickness was not related to a specific food or drink. the patern of distribution of the symptoms hinted for a larger, common source. i beleive that the hurricane dammaged the water-treatement plant or infrastructure rendering it less than optimal. it is the only way i can explain wide-ranging contamination.besides, at 160us$ per patient, the doctor and the hotel made a nice sum treating patients...okay, these were the subjective aspects of my trip.service:service was generally great, people were friendly and always in good spirits and sported the world-famous Payloads: best place to stay for access to children's hospital boston we just returned from boston, ma, having stayed at this hotel for 10 days. our son underwent surgery at children's hospital boston and we needed accomodations near the facility. the hotel is less than one block away from the hospital, and within walking distance to many other attractions as well as the public transportation system. it is about a $30 cab ride from logan international airport. the front desk was kind enough to realize the length of our stay, and gave us a very spacious room along with complimentary crib for my son. with the exception of frequent ambulances (which can't be helped), the room was very quiet. housekeeping was fantastic. the hotel is also conveniently attached to a mall food court, so we had easy access to multiple take-out options. there is a cvs pharmacy within the complex which was very convenient. the hotel offers an exceptional children's hospital rate, and then also reduced the rate because we had an extended stay. if we need to return for further medical care, we will certainly stay here again.

Payloads: great family atmosphere we stayed at this resort for for three days in july. we live in the phoenix area and took advantage of the reasonable summer rates. our family of four stayed in a cassita. this is a two story townhouse suite. there was plenty of room for everyone. the suites come with one or two bedrooms upstairs and an upstairs bathroom. downstairs,there is a pull out couch , kitchen with a sink, fridge and microwave. the hotel will supply a cot if additional bedding is needed. this resort also has motel room suites. our two boys, ages 11 and 13 really enjoyed themselves here. there was plenty to do at the western themed pool areasuch as tubing on the lazy river, basketball at the sport pool or miniature golfing. ask for the value pack to save money on the miniature golfing and fitness club .there was also a saturday night movie at the pool area for the younger kiddies. they might want to set up a pg-13 movie at the sport pool area. this is an older resort that is kept up pretty well. the pool area needs some kind of pebbletec path to avoid burning your feet and there wasn't a safe in our suite. this can be a big problem when the whole family goes out to the pool. the resort is very close to the camelback area where there are additional places to dine. fashion square mall is down the street as well. we had a great time!

Payloads: loved it and would stay again in a heartbeat! we were very hesitant to stay here given the plethora of bad reviews, but we were more than pleased with our stay.we found a booking code on travelzoo for 119 per night. while this got us the cheapest tower room, the check-in clerk upgraded us to a cabana pool room! the desk and concierge were all very nice and helpful to us.the room was huge and clean with a very comfortable bed and great bathroom. the clerk made it clear upon check-in that as a hotel guest we were permitted to bring up to three guests to the tropicana bar. the policy was clearly stated by them and upheld by the tropicana staff. we decided to go have a drink at the bar and we found all of the staff very nice and courteous. we really don't understand all of the bad reviews about the rude service.we also ate at the in-house dakota restaurant and absolutely loved it! we each had a kobe steak and it was one of the tastiest steaks we've ever had in our lives (and we've had kobe steak in kobe). the restaurant staff were also friendly.yes, the lobby of the hotel is dark - but it's massive and moorish architecture. it's true to its past. it is what it is and we felt it would have been a shame to turn the lights up and ruin the atmosphere and architecture.the hotel has two laptops with free internet connections in the check-in area which we thought was a great nice touch.the hotel is also only about a block from the hollywood/highland center and the metro stop there. for all of those who say don't take the metro we disagree! we thought it was great! we took the flyaway bus from lax to union station and the metro the rest of the way to the hotel. it only cost us $4.50! two weeks later we stayed at the hotel mosaic in beverly hills which uniformly receives good reviews on tripadvisor. we agree that it is a great hotel, but we liked the hollywood roosevelt more! all in all we loved it. maybe the management has gotten the message, or maybe everyone who stays there hoping to see a celebrity and doesn't writes bad reviews. whatever the reason, we disagree with the bad reviews.

(much better than the way they hound you in mexico.)we would definately stay there again.

Payloads: for downtown omni is tops this was second stay at omni. first stay was in september 2007. on both occasions i enjoyed it. good clean room, discrete but warm service. it's a bland hotel but there is a good feel to the place architecturally - even though it is not special there is good natural light, layout seems sensible - more like an apartment block than a hotel. also the staff are not sycophantic. fitness room is great, didn't use the pool. car parking is a rip-off but you can park overnight in any of the local places including pershing square for much less $ and walk two blocks. great location for the gehry, moca, la phil and so on. i have also stayed at the westin bonaventure and the orchid hotel in downtown and this has the best all round mix of atmosphere, comfort and amenities.

Payloads: affinia doalot it could be called.... as we stayed here just recently while in town for a long weekend. the management team is supurb here and the accomodations are some of the biggest - space-wise - that you will find in nyc. as usual we booked our stay on expedia.com, and upon checking on their website for our confirmation # less than 24 hours before check-in, we realized that the rate for our junior suite room had dropped. the expedia agent called the hotel and spoke with the front desk manager and the manager waived the cancellation fee and we rebooked at the lower rate. this was a positive and exceeded my expectations on what the hotel may do as a result of our inquiry. checking in was a breeze. we encountered a couple of problems with the room service and also the smoking (the hotel is all non-smoking) - and a barking dog (the hotel is very pet friendly so you may hear this during your stay) in the room directly across the hall from us - but all was taken care of upon my bringing it to the manager's attention. we were promptly re-located to another room (junior suite) on a higher floor (29 vs. 18). the view from 29 is amazing - if you can imagine - as you can see the chrysler tower to the north and the east river to the east.....it's breathtaking both during the day and even more so at night. the hotel room itself is huge - as stated before - bigger than most even beyond the big apple. most / or all junior suites i was told are in the corners...giving you ample room and the view i spoke of. the amenities are first rate in the room, an umbrella stand with an umbrella, and aveda toiletries. i was impressed. the decor could use a minimal up

Payloads: the staff and location was perfect! it was our first trip away from canada so we were a little scared and new at the whole traveling bit. needless to say our luggage somehow lost us on the way and we showed up at the hotel around 1am with nothing. we let the front desk know about our luggage and we were told it would be all taken care of should our luggage show up. the hotel staff offered us toothbrushes, toothpaste and other amenities to tide us over until morning. the hotel is right across the street from bayside market - perfect location!! we had a ton of fun eating, shopping and eating some more. when our luggage showed up the hotel tucked it away nicely for us and waited for us to get back to the hotel. check out was quick!cons: the view wasn't the best, we looked onto a parking lot...but hey, we were going on a cruise in a couple of days so we didn't care. the only issue we had with the room was the sound of a clock on the street - some grandfather sounding thing...bing bonging at 5am...not so great when we didn't get to sleep until at least 230am.rather far to malls - paid $40 to get to dolphin mall

Payloads: wonderful resort for relaxing vacation just got home from a vacation at punta cana all-suites resort and spa. stayed from june 26 to july 3rd. went with my husband and 2 children (3 12 y.o.) . went to punta cana last year. we stayed then at breezes. we enjoyed both locations, but pcprincess is a muched more relaxed location. there are only about 250 rooms compared to breezes with over 700. there were fewer activities for the kids, but they could do the kids club. additionally, if you book the vip service you have access to the other two resorts next door owned by princess. they have many more activities. however you will notice the difference when you visit there. it is quite busy and loud. it is was too noisy compared to pcprincess. we only went over there to go to la cava italian restaurant (excellent).the beach at this location were absolutely beautiful. we were able to walk in either direction to the local vendors. this was fun, but they are very aggressive. i am not the type that enjoys a tough negotiation (i felt they got annoyed when you didn't buy). only go if you are up for the challenge of trying to negotiate a bargan. most of the time i felt i was being ripped off. still they had some nice jewelry, and beach cover-ups we wore the entire stay. the beach offers all types of water sports, banana boat, snorkeling, parasailing, etc. we chose to relax at the beach. you can buy sand toys at the pcprincess minimarket, $9 us. the kids liked the pool the best. we could barely get them out. we were there from 9am to 5pm most days. they loved it. rooms were clean and of good size. checkin was smooth.food was good. it is not what you are commonly used to eating at home. we made the most of it. they were more than willing to try to accomo

Payloads: loved stanford court my husband and i stayed in this hotel for 3 nights while we were visiting san francisco. we had a great stay in this hotel. only complains are the water pressure was slow from the sink faucet and the valet fees are a little high. our room was on the 5th floor facing to powell and we saw the cable car . it also has a nice view. we heard some street noise on the first night since it was sat. sun was a little quiet or may be we got used to the noise, it did not bother us much. starbucks coffee is a nice touch in the morning especially my husband is a coffee person. we missed the champagne since we were always out during that time. the hotel room had no fridge. but we requested one. the front desk staff was very nice and also greeted us. we borrowed an umbrella from the concierge since it was raining on one of the nights. the valet parking service was very good and staff was very friendly as well. the court yard of the hotel is big (not on the street) so we did not feel rush when we dropped off the car for valet service. we walked to union square. going there was easy. coming back was hard since we had to walk up to the hill. but we enjoyed the walk. we also walked to chinatown and tadich grill for dinner. be prepared to involve a lot of climbings if you are not using car/cable car.

Payloads: grand at first blush, but the rooms, service, and extra costs ruin the value this historic hotel is grand in its common areas, and by the looks of the room and the service the hotel is targeting the rental of its meeting rooms rather than its services as a hotel for travelers. don't be fooled by their website photos. the photos do not provide an accurate overall picture of the environment. we generally use the choice hotels' clarion, but decided to go for something out of the ordinary to make the trip more exciting. bad decision. the true cost of your stay is not reflected in the rate, because they will charge you for every service you use. rooms: dingy and in dire need of repairs/upgrades. once we entered our room we were certain that we were in a 2 star hotel. repairs to the tile, plumbing, and fixtures looked like they had been performed by the bellhop. the workmanship and materials were low grade. tile grout had been replaced with poorly installed silicone caulk--ultra cheap. services: $9.95 for 24 hrs. of internet access. free internet access is something i have come to take for granted. another mistake. the good news, the la library is just a half a block away and offers free internet access to the public. great walking destination after breakfast or early dinner. the hotel charges for local calls $1 each. the hotel charges for toll-free calls, $1 each. linens: terrible. the sheets were thin and so were the pillows. towels were thick and nice.parking: $32 per day. i am not a fan of giving my car over to strangers, or being gouged for parking, so we parked across the street each evening for $14 in the underground parking garage which felt safe and secure and is little further from the elevators than is the hotel's driveway valet drop off.pool exercise room: the pool has a classic look with tile throughout with an attractive brass railing all around. unfortunately, it is very small. with three other people in the pool we felt it was too crowded to get in. also, the floor surrounding the pool was dirty. the exercise equipment might have been installed for the hotel's original grand opening in the 30s. and it is crammed into much less space than is needed to enjoy your workout. restaurants: we ate at smeraldi's the first night. food was good, the service very slow. the prices were reasonable. the second evening we stopped in what the hotel touts as downtown la's hottest sports bar. it must be downtown la's only sports bar, then. and it is not open on sundays. uh, don't most sporting events occur on sunday? anyway, the food was poor, the beer was warm and the service was very slow. we actually had to get up from the table and go to the bar to ask for drink refills. the environment was dark and dreary, but there are plenty of televisions, if you want to watch a game.all-in-all this is a lousy place to stay, whatever the cost, and the final cost is far too high for the accommodations. not a good value.

Payloads: we stayed longer than planned!! my husband and i went to a convention in town and only planned to stay at the hotel and in that area of san francisco for 4 days. (even though our flight was for a week stay) we ended up extending our entire stay with the tuscan. we loved the ease of running in and out of our room for pit stops. we joked about the rooms being sound proof since we never heard other guests and we slept great. we asked the staff to empty the refrigerator and snack bar so we could stock our own items, they did it easily and quickly. we ate breakfast nearly every morning at the attached restaurant. they have fantastic omelets, fresh fruit, real home fries etc...we didn't have a chance to try lunch or dinner there. we would love to go back to san francisco and we would definitely stay at best western tuscan again. we used public transportation for the first 4 days and rented a car for the last 3 days (we wanted to explore the outskirts of the city) budget rental didn't have a fee for dropping the car off at the airport like some of the other companies (plus the car was nice/new). on bad notes of our vacation: we rented a 3 wheel go cart that made so much noise and the exhaust smell almost made us sick. 2nd bad note was we felt that the hotel was not helpful/knowledgeable in recommending restaurants. make sure to have dinner from a city view restaurant at night (window view of course).

Payloads: kids suite a plus...for kids... we had originally booked a king bedroom and upon arriving with our very active 2 year old, they offered to upgrade us to a kids suite which includes twin bunkbeds in the kids area and a queen bed for the grownups. it seemed like a good idea and we eventually made it work for us with some mishaps and adjustments. this suite is for kids, toddlers only if you are forewarned. basically, these are baby proofing issues that are not the norm for older kids. as always with toddlers, lots and lots of supervision is necessary. most hotel cribs are too small for a toddler so she would have ended up sleeping with us in a normal room (hence the king). we ended up having to go out to buy a safety rail so she could sleep in the lower twin. once the safety rail was in place, everthing was fine. the reading lights attached to the wall for the bunk beds get very hot, and curious 2 year olds can burn their fingers. i ended up unplugging the whole contraption. you have to put the latch over the door, because even locked, they can get out and they are off. then, if the latch is on and they try to open the door they could get their hand/fingers caught if the door closes. ah, yes and the bunkbeds. on day 3, she discovered the ladder...it is not detachable.now for the plusses. yes, there are quite a few. the queen bed was very comfortable. being able to put our daughter to bed in a separate area of the room and still read or watch tv was a real treat after other hotel stays. the restaurant food and service were very nice and other than the usual hassle of dining with a toddler, we enjoyed ourselves. the staff was very helpful, friendly, polite, etc. we got plenty of clean towels, the hotel was clean and attractive, the grounds were pleasant and attractive. there is a grocery store within walking distance if you need supplies, not just a minimart. room service was handled well. one minus outside of the kid stuff. the terrace outside our room was on the highway side of hotel. the road noise was unbelievable. i only opened the doors once. that was enough. fortunately, the terrace doors are sound proofed, i think. the terrace would have been nice otherwise (except i'm sure my daughter would have tried to climb the railings and i would have had to close them anyway).the splash pool adjacent to the regular pool was the perfect depth for our daughter. she was able to stand with the water chest high and after getting more familiar with it, enjoyed herself tremendously several times during our stay. of course, most of the time i was in there with her, the rest of the time, i sat on the edge with my feet in. the diameter was about the size of a small hot tub. unfortunately, i learned they were considering converting to a hot tub. overall, we really did enjoy our stay. if i had older children, the kids suite would have been awesome.

Payloads: fantastic stay and fantastic city we stayed here for 5 nights at the beginning of november. it was a fantastic hotel - great location in one of the posher areas of san francisco. it was a 10 min max walk downhill to union square and you can get the cable car back up for $5 - but we mostly walked this as it is manageable.san fran is a great city. must dos are going to the cheesecake factory to eat at the top of macy's. great views and gorgeous food. we took two bus tours of the city also - one for the downtown area and the other over the golden gate bridge. my advice is to book alcatraz before you come out as it gets booked up really quickly - they only let a relatively small number over everyday - but it means it's not at all crowded when you're over there. book the early bird tour. it's a fascinating, eerie place to walk around and you can stay on the island as long as you want once you're out there.if you want to go out for the evening, we had a great night out in little italy. some fab italian restaurants and bars. everyone is really friendly and we met some great people - including some virgin atlantic crew who were also staying at the stanford court whilst in san fran!would definitely stay there again and recommend it to anyone. the beds were so comfy and our room was at the back so it was very quiet. the breakfast was very expensive so we always ate out - there's lori's diner 2 blocks away, so that was never a problem. the room was massive (2 double beds) but i agree that the bathroom was a little dated - everything in working order though.if you're wondering whether or not to go to san fran - do it! it's a wonderful place - great shops, lovely restaurants and friendly people.

Payloads: enjoyed our stay at the omni but not sure about its location i booked this hotel because of the recommendations on this website but i did not feel as strongly in its favour as other people had done. on arrival by car it was quite difficult to access because of the one way system. our room was lovely. it was large with excellent amenities although the bathroom was showing its age. after checking in we went for a walk to have a look at the surrounding area. we walked downhill to the jewellery district and i did not feel safe in this area. there were several people sleeping rough on the streets and one was shouting abuse at passing pedestrians. i was glad to get back to the hotel and considered moving to another hotel the next night. on a plus side the hotel is very handy for the theatres (they are in the opposite direction) and we went to see jersey boys which was excellent. we found the staff very pleasant and the buffet breakfast was excellent. we also had a meal in noe restaurant and this was excellent. the hotel is at california plaza and there is an area where open air concerts take place. this is very enjoyable and many locals come along to enjoy the music. if this hotel had been situated in a different area i would have enjoyed it more but i did not feel comfortable venturing far from the hotel particularly at night.

Payloads: lovely evening we stayed in a suite at the tuscan inn the weekend before thanksgiving. i certainly would recommend a suite for parties of 3 or more. (i traveled with my wife and teenage son.) the rooms' furniture and amenities were quite nice.the afternoon wine party was well-attended and pleasant. we had pizza hors d'oeuvres. the continental breakfast is inadequate (only tiny biscotti are provided). we ate dinner at the cafe pescatore (the on-line site restaurant). our meals were ok; however, i have never been impressed with restaurants in the fisherman's wharf area.after dinner we walked to pier 39 and enjoyed the sea lions and the atmosphere.

Payloads: terrible service!! it was so bad i had to write this review...save yourself. i read the reviews on trip advisor before we went and we should have known better. don't book this hotel -- you have been warned. first of all, they are understaffed. i'm not looking to be waited on hand-and-foot, but you have to wait in line for everything. did i tell you there wasn't a beach? the water is very cloudy and almost dirty there. one mile away they have a great public beach....they won't tell you that there though.to stop me from ranting i will just include bullet points:- there are no waiters, you have to wait in line to get anything. wait in line to get a hamburger from the pool bar. you have to wait in line to get a drink at any bar and by the way, they are doing you a favor to get you a drink. tip them and they don't move any faster (i tipped one waiter $50 -- keep your tip).- the place is very spread out and therefore, once in a while you want to take a shuttle service (e.g., forgot the sunscreen) back to your room. forget it. the shuttle service is random and almost non-existent. it may be a 8 minute walk to just get to the pool -- don't forget anything!!- we had to wait in line even at the buffet restuarant! the food was ok and sometimes very good. that was one plus. don't get the steaks - -they are very tough. - the check-in took two hours. we wanted a couple of rooms next to eachother, but we got rooms with our party located in opposite sides of the resort. i called multiple times to confirm we would be next to our friends during check-in. didn't happen and the staff didn't care.- don't take the hotel shuttle to the airport. they charge you way too much for this trip. they don't tell you the price and in fact, they act like the shuttle service is free to use. use a taxi van and you will save yourself at least $100 for a party of four.- the water toys at the hotel are almost useless because the hotel is located on a shelf that has a break reef about 100 yards from the shore. nobody can pass this breaker wall and therefore, you are stuck in mucky water that is shallow and full of leaves and seaweed -- let alone the rocks that hurt our kids feet and mine.- the beds were soft..huge plus for an island hotel. this was a postive surprise. however, back to the staffing -- the cleaning help barely cleaned your room. they would change the sheets and that was about it. they wouldn't even sweep, or move your shoes, to sweep under them.overall, the staff takes on the management's attitude. i never complained to the management once, but i heard multiple parties that did call them and complained about the above items. you can join them and go to this hotel, or learn the hard way. this is the first time i used trip advisor and i will be sure to up

Payloads: Loved the Affinia - great location for a girls getaway! I went to NYC with 3 girlfriends for a long weekend getaway (Feb 14 - 18). NYC hotel rooms are notoriously tiny, so with 4 girls in one room, we wanted a hotel with a spacious room, and it had to be in a convenient and safe location. Affinia 50 did not disappoint! We got the studio suite, which had 2 queen beds, a kitchen, and a huge hallway where we could drop all our luggage. The bathroom was ok - fits a bathtub and a small sink (no counter). The hotel caters mostly to business travellers, so it was important for the rooms to be spacious, comfy and cozy.Good things about Affinia 50:1) The room (as discussed above) - you do have to pay an extra $10 per person per night if you have more than 2 people in the room. But since we were splitting the cost bewteen 4 people, it still came out to a very reasonable rate. 2) The location - the subway was 2 small blocks away, we could walk to Chrysler Building and Rockefeller Center along with all the Fifth Avenue stores. Many little cafes, restaurants and grocery stores if you need to grab a bite on the go. Very convenient!!3) Amenities - there are complimentary cocktail receptions in the evenings (on weeknights), a club lounge on the 2nd floor, a fitness center, and most impressively - a pillow menu! The hotel offers 6 different types of pillows for you to try to guarantee a sound sleep. We tried the Swedish memory foam and the magnetic pillow - we had a great sleep every night! 4) Service - the front desk and the bell boy were all very helpful regardng transportation, restaurants and clubbing recommendations. The bell boy even came up to look at our leaky fridge (see below) as soon as I went downstairs to complain.Not so good things:1) Kitchen - the kitchen is very convenient, but the appliances are slightly out

Payloads: nice, convenient hotel we stayed for 4 nights mid october, in a suite to cater for 2 couples. the first room we had was kinda worn, no view, and you could hear noisy a/c units, and the beds felt worn, as you could feel the springs if you pressed firmly!! not good! unfortunately, i had come down with a rather nasty throat infection on this, the 2nd leg of our extensive trip, coming from 5 nights in santa monica, la. anyway, the next morning i requested another room with either a street or garden courtyard view.big difference! the room we got was bigger, toward the rear of the building, so a long walk from lift, but well worth it. it also had a pleasant courtyard view. this room also felt as if it had been used maybe a third as much as the other one!! perhaps they like to let out all the 'close to lift ' rooms to be kind to housekeeping?!? biggest difference though - the beds - no uncomfortable springs!! also, the bathrooms were quite well set up, with a seperate toilet/shower to basin, so whilst one guest is showering another can use the basin.decor etc. was quite nice and fresh looking, and it is because of this that i would not hesitate to come back - provided i got a similar room! internet provided via a pc in foyer was very handy!!only thing i missed was a gym, for some reason i had an inclination to use the gyms while we were o/s!? service was all good, albeit a bit stoic. i was dutifully helped at 130am when i wanted a hospital to nip my sickness in the bud, which was much appreciated. however, i felt a little weird, almost uncomfortable when on a couple of nights, whilst suffering coughing fits, i decided to go downstairs and use the internet, so as to not keep my fellow guests awake. upon arriving downstairs, i found the duty manager/staff napping on the (guest?) lounges !!. it didn't bother me, but felt a little weird, like i was interrupting them!! anyways, one night we came back just after they had turned off the coffee machine in the restaurant, but the wonderful waiter/maitre'd organised some hot drinks for us in the biggest mugs i've ever seen - legend!!! we all loved san fran - fantastic city with great selection of restaurants etc, fishermans wharf was great also - ate at wipeout, where the waiters were very honest with what to order!! ate at caesars old style italian - fantastic for price, and also mona lisa on columbus in awesome little italy. unfortunately we didn't get to dine in the hotel restaurant, but i'd say it would be good, if the after hours service is anything to go by! can't wait to go back to sf and explore some more, i.e.berkely sausalito etc. if you like architectural history do the 'ghost tour' from queen anne hotel...fantastic, intriguing history in most exclusive area of city.the hotel is nice and close to fishermans wharf and other attractions, which was really handy.

Payloads: one would expect much more! i have booked this hotel via british airways and ba e-mailed them, i e-mailed them several times with my simple requests regarding a quiet room with good views. miranda in reservations said no problems but what i have experienced was completely different.the hotel's common areas on the ground floor are simly majestic (a mixture between alphonso xiii in seville and nacional de cuba in havana). however this is where the beauty stops, as my room had no views (imagine a u shaped wall and my window at the base at the u - limited views). the most upsetting though after spending all this time on e-mails was the room location on a busy hallway. it was very difficult to sleep (after a 11h flight and 8h difference with london) with all the disconsiderate young girls shouting on the hallway up to 3am la time (the doors were so thin), nevermind the engine like permanent noise that came from somewhere outside (probably underground) that made even things in the bathroom vibrate). the room did not have double glazing was very basic and looks like a 2 or 3 star hotel. i was offered a room on the next floor but just above, so probably the same problems. at 4am i went to the business room to print 2 pages that cost me together with 6min spent online the amount of almost 7 dollars (could be pricey for the americans). it seems to me the hotel would more suit a big noisy group and not quiet tired people. the receptionist said the hotel does not have plans for a future renovation (the bathroom would definitely benefit). at 7am i checked out and just after 8am i was comfortably checked in beverly hilton (that's what i call outstanding service). based on the lack of sleep and presentation i would rate my experience as terrible and the hotel as a 3 star only.

Payloads: great value! stayed at the adante hotel from 7/29 thru 8/1 and were very impressed with the value of this budget hotel. i was somewhat skeptical and paranoid about the location being on the edge of the tenderloin district but the location turned out to be excellent. we hauled suitcases at 9:30 at night from the powell street station up to the hotel with absolutely no problems. had two teenager with us, quite an eye opener for them with all the hustle bustle and happenings on the street. the hotel itself was very clean, unique and friendly. i suppose you could pay the same and stay at a holiday inn but you would be experiencing cookie cutter boredom. not so at the adante. our room was small but adequate and did i mention clean? our room faced geary so it was noisy if the windows were left open but we closed them at night and ran the ceiling fan and this was more than comfy and i sleep hot. the front desk was friendly and helpful, the continental breakfast is good enough to hold you over til you can get some real breakfast. dont expect luxury, but for what you pay you will be more than pleasantly surprised!!!

Payloads: orchid suites hollywood i've stayed in some excellent locations, but it is hard to beat this one. barely 30 seconds walk to the hollywood highland centre. 3 minute walk to red line metro, 90 seconds to starbucks, etc. the rooms are an excellent size with kitchen, living area, bedroom and bathroom.staff varied in terms of helpfulness and friendliness. no one was rude but one particular lady did annoy me who continued to chat on the phone whilst serving me. my biggest complaint was to do with general upkeep. some small repairs did need to be undertaken in our room (104). hole in bed blanket. very top bit missing off cold tap. tap drips. hairdryer didn't work. we did mention this to reception but nothing got done to correct problem. toilet became blocked easily, i was given a plunger. wireless internet worked fine in living room, but the signal was too weak to use in bedroom. overall i might stay here again. if you want a bed for the night in a great location stay here, if you want anything more look for somewhere else.note: to get to the hotel from the hollywood highlands metro station the easiest route is to turn right out of the station. pass a couple of shops. you'll then be at the entrance to hollywood highlands centre. go up escalator to level 2 then head left across courtyard. pass kodak shop on your right and take exit tunnel next to kodak shop. on walking out on to the street you'll see the hotel diagonally left of you.
